title: Oct 28 Results: When the Model Misses the Mark
summary: A tough day at the office—breaking down what went wrong on Oct 28

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About Bad Days

Look, I'm not going to sugarcoat this one. October 28th was a rough day for our predictions. Sometimes the baseball gods have other plans, and today was one of those days where our model and reality didn't exactly see eye to eye.

## The Only Game in Town

With just one game on the slate, we had all our focus on Brewers at Rays. We liked Tampa Bay with a 57% confidence level—not overwhelming, but enough to lean their way. The Brewers, though? They had other ideas.

## What Happened?

The beauty and heartbreak of baseball is that a 57% probability still means the other team wins 43% of the time. That's not some distant possibility—it's nearly a coin flip. The Brewers came in as underdogs and proved exactly why you play the games instead of just running the numbers.

Our model considered the pitching matchups, home field advantage, recent form—all the usual suspects. But baseball has a funny way of humbling even the most sophisticated predictions.

content.title: 💭 The Reality Check
content.value: Even our best picks will fail 40-45% of the time
content.sub: That's the nature of baseball—and why we keep improving our model

content.value:
## Looking Ahead

Here's where I wish I had better news: there are no games scheduled for tomorrow. So we'll take this miss, learn from it, and come back stronger when the action returns.

Days like this remind us why we do what we do. It's not about being perfect—it's about being transparent, learning from the misses, and constantly refining our approach. Every wrong prediction teaches us something, and this one's going into the data bank.

We'll be back soon with fresh predictions and renewed energy. Until then, thanks for sticking with us through the ups and downs. That's what makes this journey worth taking.
